{{Recipe}}

'''Iresi eyin''' is one of the Yoruba versions of a palm oil rice dish also called palm oil rice/native Jollof rice. It is more accurately described as a palm oil rice. It is different from Yoruba jollof/Yoruba Party Jollof/ Nigerian jollof, which is more popular. It is very nutritious and easy to prepare—all that is required is to mix the ingredients together in a pot.

== Ingredients ==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Units of measurement#Nigeria|milk cups]] of [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 2 cooking spoons [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Locust Bean|locust beans]]
* 2 tbsp dried [[Cookbook:Ground Crayfish|ground crayfish]] 
* [[Cookbook:Dryfish|Dried]] [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]], or any other dried fish, soaked in hot salted water until soft, then shredded
* Pepper powder, to taste
* [[Cookbook:Chopping|Chopped]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* 1 sachet (50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* [[Cookbook:Carrot|Carrots]], washed and chopped, to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pea|Peas]], washed and parboiled if necessary, to taste
== Procedure ==
# Wash the rice and [[Cookbook:Parboiling|parboil]] for about 8 minutes. Drain and set aside.
# Heat the palm oil in a large, clean pot until the oil changes color.
# Add the locust beans, onions, tomato paste, dry pepper, and a little water. [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] until the odour of the sauce changes and becomes more fragrant.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] over medium heat for about 25 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and everything is cooked.
